L2: ENROLLING SOON
L3: # A clinical study for dogs with hemangiosarcoma
L4: 
L5: If your dog has recently been diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, our clinical study at the University of Illinois Veterinary Hospital in Urbana may be an option, and there is no cost to take part. The study is testing FAM-010, a new investigational chemotherapy designed to be gentler on the heart. Your dog may be eligible if they recently had their spleen removed or have surgery scheduled.
L6: 
L7: [Button: Contact the study team]
L8: 【1†Image: A calm dog resting its head on a bed while a person gently pets it.】
L9: ## What is hemangiosarcoma?
L10: 
L11: Hemangiosarcoma is an aggressive cancer that starts in the blood vessels, most often in the spleen. It often shows few signs until a tumor bleeds, so many dogs are diagnosed suddenly, sometimes in an emergency.
L12: 
L13: Treatment usually starts with surgery to remove the spleen, followed by chemotherapy. Even with both, the cancer often comes back, and there is still no FDA-approved treatment for hemangiosarcoma in dogs.
L14: ## How is FAM-010 different?
L15: 
L16: Doxorubicin is the current standard chemotherapy for dogs with hemangiosarcoma after surgery. But it can also reach and damage healthy tissues, especially the heart. This limits the total amount of chemotherapy a dog can receive.
L17: 
L18: FAM-010 is a new form of doxorubicin, designed to carry more of the medicine to the cancer and less of it to the heart. We hope this will let dogs receive more of the treatment they need, more safely.
L19: ## What will this study tell us?
L20: 
L21: This first study will find the right dose of FAM-010 for dogs: the highest dose they can receive without side effects becoming too much. Every dog in the study receives FAM-010, given as a short infusion every three weeks at the University of Illinois, and the study team monitors each dog closely throughout.
L22: 
L23: FAM-010 is investigational and not approved by FDA for dogs. This study is designed to establish the dose and understand its side effects.
L24: 
L25: STUDY ELIGIBILITY
L26: ## Could this study be an option for your dog?
L27: 
L28: If the following apply to your dog, we encourage you to contact us. Our study team will review your dog’s medical history and test results to confirm eligibility.
L29: 
L30:   * ### Diagnosis
L31: 
L32: A pathology report has confirmed hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, or you are waiting for the result.
L33: 
L34:   * ### Recent spleen surgery
L35: 
L36: Your dog has had their spleen removed or has surgery scheduled.
L37: 
L38:   * ### Timing
L39: You are able to travel to the study site in Urbana Illinois within 21 days after surgery.
L40: 
L41:   * ### Previous treatment
L42: 
L43: Your dog has not received chemotherapy, radiation or another investigational drug.
L44: 
L45:   * ### Travel to Urbana, Illinois
L46: 
L47: You could bring your dog to Urbana for regular study visits.
L48: 
L49:   * ### Breeding
L50: 
L51: Your dog is not intended for breeding.
L52: 
L53: Wondering if your dog might qualify?
L54: Filling out the form doesn’t commit you to anything. Tell us a little about your dog, and if the study looks like a fit, we’ll connect you with the University of Illinois study team to confirm eligibility and answer your questions.
L55: 
L56: [Button: Contact the study team]
L57: 
L58: Ask about the study
L59: ## Tell us a little about your dog and how to reach you.
L60: 
L61: Asking about the study does not enroll your dog or commit you to taking part.
L62: 
L63: [Button: Contact the study team]
L64: 
L65: Questions about the study
L66: ## A cancer diagnosis brings a lot of decisions at once.
L67: 
L68: If your dog has been diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma, this study could give them access to a new investigational treatment at no cost to you, with close care from the veterinary team at the University of Illinois.
L69: 
L70: [Button: Contact the study team]
L71: 
L72: Why might I consider this study for my dog?
L73: You may want to consider it if you and your veterinarian are looking at care options after hemangiosarcoma diagnosis and after spleen surgery. Your dog would receive the study drug and be monitored by the oncology team at Illinois, with study care paid for by Familiar. Taking part also helps researchers learn whether FAM-010 should be studied further for dogs with hemangiosarcoma. Our study team can help you understand how the study compares with other options for your dog.
L74: What would my dog and I need to do?
L75: 
L76: You would bring your dog to Urbana about every three weeks for treatment and health checks. The initial course is planned for six treatments over about three and a half months. Some dogs may receive up to twelve treatments. There are also follow-up calls and visits after treatment ends. Before you decide, our study team will explain the full schedule and what each visit involves.
L77: 
L78: Will my dog receive FAM-010?
L79: Yes. Every dog that joins this study receives FAM-010. There is no placebo. Dogs enter in small groups, and the dose may differ between groups as the team learns what dogs can tolerate.
L80: 
L81: Could FAM-010 improve survival for dogs with hemangiosarcoma?
L82: 
L83: We hope it could. That is one reason we are studying it. This first study focuses on the dose dogs can tolerate and the side effects they experience. Our study team can discuss the study alongside other care options for your dog.
L84: My dog's pathology result is not back yet. Should I wait to get in touch?
L85: 
L86: No. You can ask about the study now, especially because the first dose must be given within 21 days after surgery. Our study team will need to confirm the diagnosis before your dog can join.
L87: 
L88: Is this study safe for my dog?
L89: Because FAM-010 is investigational, we are still learning what side effects dogs may have at different doses. Our study team will assess your dog's health before enrollment, monitor your dog during treatment and explain the known and possible risks before you decide. They can also discuss those risks alongside other care options for your dog.
L90: 
L91: Why might my dog not be able to join, even if they qualify?
L92: Dogs enter in small groups so our study team can review side effects before studying the next dose. A pause may mean the next group cannot begin within 21 days after your dog's surgery. If that happens, we will tell you rather than leave you waiting.
L93: 
L94: What would I pay for?
L95: 
L96: Familiar covers the full participation in the clinical trial including study screening, treatment and follow-up care. Your only cost associated with taking part is travel to and from the hospital in Urbana.
L97: Can a dog that has not been spayed or neutered take part?
L98: 
L99: Possibly, but dogs intended for breeding cannot join. FAM-010 is expected to cause permanent infertility in male dogs that have not been neutered. Our study team will explain what this means for your dog before you decide.
L100: 
L101: Can I change my mind after my dog joins?
L102: 
L103: Yes. You can choose to stop your dog's participation. Our study team will discuss your dog's ongoing care with you.
L104: 
L105: Who is Familiar Therapeutics?
L106: Familiar is an animal health company developing medicines for dogs and cats. We are developing FAM-010 and sponsoring this study. Veterinarians at the University of Illinois are responsible for evaluating dogs, explaining the study and providing their care during it.
L107: 
L108: About this study: Sponsored by Familiar Therapeutics and conducted at the University of Illinois Veterinary Hospital in Urbana, Illinois.

L4: # Advancing the science of veterinary therapeutics.
L5:

L61: FAM-010 · Hemangiosarcoma
L62: ## We are working toward the first FDA-approved treatment for hemangiosarcoma in dogs.
L63: 
L64: Hemangiosarcoma is one of the most aggressive cancers a dog can face. After surgery, vets usually turn to doxorubicin, a human chemotherapy that is not FDA-approved for use in dogs. It helps, but it strains the heart with every dose, so most dogs can only receive limited treatments before they have to stop, even when the cancer hasn't.
L65: ### FAM-010 is designed to be gentler on the heart, so treatment can go further
L66: 
L67: FAM-010 is a new form of doxorubicin. It is attached to albumin, a natural protein in the blood, which is designed to carry the medicine to the tumor and release it there. Because less of the medicine reaches the rest of the body, we expect FAM-010 to be less toxic than standard doxorubicin, especially to the heart.
L68: We are studying whether more medicine reaching the tumor, for a longer period of time, can potentially mean better control of the cancer and more time for dogs with the people who love them.
L69: 
L70: Who it's for
L71:     Dogs with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, after surgery
L72: 
L73: How it's given
L74:     An infusion at the vet
L75: 
L76: OUR PROGRESS
L77:     Pilot study, enrolling soon at the University of Illinois
L78: 
L79: FAM-010 is investigational and not approved by FDA. FDA approval is not guaranteed.
L80: 
L81: FAM-010 CLINICAL STUDY
L82: ## Trial enrollment is opening this fall.
L83: 
L84: Our FAM-010 pilot study opens soon at the University of Illinois, for dogs recently diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, at no cost to dog owners. Owners can check whether their dog may be eligible, and veterinarians can refer patients.

L214: # Clinical Trials
L215: 
L216: Clinical trials are research studies that try to answer specific clinical questions about new therapies and drugs. Often clinical trials offer cutting-edge treatments at a reduced cost to the animal owner. This research generates new ways to detect and treat clinical problems for the benefit of animal and human medicine.
L217: ## Current Clinical Trials
L218: 
L219: If you are interested in one of our studies, your animal will be evaluated to see if he/she is a good candidate for the study. As the animal owner, you will be asked to sign a consent form that details the study, its potential benefits and risks, and what will be asked of you/provided to you.
L220: If you’d like to get further details on a clinical trial or find out how to qualify, click on the link below for that particular trial. If you have questions about a particular study, please contact the principal investigator that is listed.
